# blkit

> A Go SDK for expressing and executing business rules and processes.

## Documentation
- [Home](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/): A Go SDK for expressing and executing business rules and processes in code.
- [Getting started](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/getting-started/): Orientation for new users — what blkit is, when to reach for it, and how to run your first example.
- [Installation](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/installation/): How to add blkit to your Go project and pin it to a known version.
- [Tutorials](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/tutorials/): Guided, narrative walkthroughs that build a working artefact step by step.
- [Templates](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/templates/): Ready-to-copy project scaffolds and boilerplate patterns for common use cases.

## Examples
- [Examples](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/): Focused, self-contained demonstrations of specific blkit features.
- [Example: Loan Eligibility](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/loan-eligibility/): A retail bank decides whether a personal loan application is approved, conditionally approved, or declined — and on what terms — from the applicant's credit profile.
- [Example: Shipping Rate Calculator](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/shipping-rate/): An e-commerce platform calculates the total shipping charge for a parcel from billable weight, destination zone, speed tier, and a fuel surcharge — composed entirely from blkit expressions.
- [Example: Order Fulfillment Process](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/order-fulfillment/): An e-commerce platform handles an order from placement through stock reservation, payment, picking, dispatch, and delivery — with explicit branches for out-of-stock and payment-failure cases.
- [Example: Employee Expense Approval](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/expense-approval/): An employee submits a business expense claim; the approval route — automatic, manager, or finance director — is determined by amount, category, and the employee's seniority, then the matching review runs.
- [Example: SaaS Subscription Pricing Engine](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/product-pricing/): A SaaS company calculates the final per-seat price and total monthly charge for a subscription from plan, billing cycle, seat count, loyalty tier, and an optional promo code — four compounding discount factors.
- [Example: Invoice Processing Workflow](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/invoice-processing/): An accounts payable team runs three concurrent validation checks on a supplier invoice, assigns GL codes, routes for amount-based approval, and schedules payment.
- [Example: Employee Onboarding](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/employee-onboarding/): When a new employee is hired, IT, HR, and Facilities run their setup tasks in parallel; the process completes only when all three signal readiness, and escalates if any misses the five-business-day deadline.
- [Example: Insurance Claim Assessment](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/insurance-claim/): A motor insurer assesses a claim's eligibility, scores the damage severity, and calculates a settlement offer — referring high-value settlements to a senior assessor.
- [Example: Customer Discount Eligibility](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/customer-discount/): A pricing engine evaluates an order against many discount rules, collects every rule that matches, and applies the single highest percentage — discounts do not stack.
- [Example: Product Return and Refund](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/product-return/): A customer requests a return; the process validates eligibility within the return window, grades the item's condition on receipt, and issues a refund, replacement, or store credit accordingly.
- [Example: Australian Personal Income Tax Calculator](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/aus-personal-income-tax/): An accounting service calculates an individual's annual income tax liability for FY 2024–25 — building taxable income from many sources, applying progressive brackets, levies, offsets, and HELP/HECS, then reconciling against amounts already paid.
